sections.h2: Where do Midland County deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street in Midland, MI 48640, and answers at (989) 832-6820. Recording runs on weekdays, opening at 8 a.m. and closing to new documents at 4 p.m. The vault, where the older books live, opens a half hour later.

A deed that shows up after the 4 p.m. cutoff waits for the next business day, and it queues in the order received as long as cash or a check came with it. The staff handle warranty and quit claim deeds, land contracts, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. They draft nothing and give no legal advice, which means a seller who still needs a deed written should see an attorney or a title company.

sections.h2: Which fees does the Midland County office list?
sections.html:
One flat $30.00 covers any document of any length, with the state remonumentation and automation charges folded in. A few extras appear on the county's own fee sheet.

Fees on the Midland County Register of Deeds sheet
ItemAmount
Recording one document$30.00
Document assigning or discharging more than one instrument$3.00 per instrument beyond the first, added to $30.00
Treasurer's tax certificate$5.00 for up to 5 legal descriptions, then $1.00 each
Plain copy$1.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00 plus $1.00 per page

Payment can be cash, a check made out to Register of Deeds, or a card at the counter, where the processor adds a charge the office puts near $1.50. The office also takes e-recording from qualified submitters, though anything needing a raised court seal or a death certificate has to be brought in on paper.

sections.h2: Which Midland County deeds need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
The county's recording page lists four instruments that require a treasurer's certificate before the register will accept them:

  • Any warranty deed, or other deed with a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • An assignment of a land contract that has a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a site condominium.

Get the certificate before closing day, because the deed cannot be recorded without it. A bare quit claim deed is missing from that list. Sellers curious about the tax status of a parcel can use the county's online lookup, which the county describes as showing what the treasurer's counter would show.

sections.h2: What does transfer tax come to under the Midland County chart?
sections.html:
The chart pairs $3.75 per $500 for the state with $0.55 per $500 for the county, which makes $4.30 per $500. A sale at $100,000 produces $750 for the state, $110 for the county and $860 overall. Any value of $100 or more triggers payment, subject to the exemptions on the two sheets the office links.

A Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit lets the parties leave the price off the deed. A separate Property Transfer Affidavit goes to the assessor of the City of Midland or of the township where the parcel lies, and state law gives the buyer 45 days to file it.

sections.h2: What is the usual order of a Midland County closing?
sections.html:
A title company runs most of these steps, but the order helps a seller see where the money and paper go.

  • Request a treasurer's tax certificate when the deed contains a warranty covenant.
  • Have the deed notarized. The recorder's staff cannot do it, and the County Clerk in the same County Services Building charges a small fee.
  • Send the state and county transfer tax to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed (MCL 207.523(3)).
  • Record the deed and pay the $30.00, aiming to arrive before 4:00 p.m.
  • Leave the buyer to file the Property Transfer Affidavit with the City of Midland or the township assessor inside the 45-day window.

Recorders also pass a list of recorded transactions to local assessors at least monthly under MCL 211.27a(10).

sections.h2: How far back do Midland County's records go?
sections.html:
The office dates its records from 1855, the year the county was established. Books and microfilm cover the whole run, scanned images with computer indexing start in 1968, and online images reach back to 1950. Searches run through Fidlar-hosted tools called Tapestry EON and Laredo, and anyone may order a copy of a recorded paper, since all of them are public.

The index for 1958 to 1968 is available in an Adobe search format, and entries older than 1958 turn up in the Simple Search option. The office says back-indexing continues, so an older chain of title may need a visit or a call. The county's recording page also links a property fraud alert and a reporting form, which is worth asking about if a relative's name is still on a parcel you plan to sell.

sections.h2: What does the ground and water situation look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Midland County has 517 square miles of land by the Census Bureau's count and only two incorporated cities, Midland, the county seat, and Coleman. The Tittabawassee River runs through Edenville Township and past the village of Sanford. In May 2020 the Edenville and Sanford dam failures forced evacuations across parts of the city, the village and several townships, so a seller near the river should be ready to answer flood and drainage questions in writing. Dow Chemical dates to 1890 in the city of Midland, per the county history.

Service lines vary by location. The city of Midland provides water and sewer to its residents and a few neighboring townships, while parcels beyond municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems. Winters are cold and snowy, with January highs near freezing. Out in the townships, collect well and septic records before listing.

sections.h2: How does Midland County's housing stock compare in the Census data?
sections.html:
For 2025 the Bureau estimates 83,754 residents in 37,723 housing units. Owners hold 78.1 percent of occupied homes, so roughly 22 percent are rented, at a median gross rent of $1,016. The typical owner-occupied home was valued at $195,400 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income was $77,705. Builders took out 128 permits in 2025.

The county's headcount is up just 0.3 percent from the April 2020 base. About 90 percent of residents stayed in the same house for the prior year, which points to long ownership. Workers average 23.7 minutes to reach their jobs, and 36.6 percent of adults 25 or older have a bachelor's degree.

faqs.q: What is the street address for Midland County deeds?
faqs.a: 220 W Ellsworth Street, Midland, MI 48640, phone (989) 832-6820. Recording closes at 4 p.m. on weekdays, and papers received later are recorded the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the price to file a deed there?
faqs.a: $30.00 for any document, regardless of length. A treasurer's tax certificate for a warranty deed adds $5.00 for up to five legal descriptions.

faqs.q: Does Midland County take e-recorded deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, from qualified submitters, including documents that need tax certification. Paper is still required for documents that need a raised court seal or a death certificate.

faqs.q: Can the register's staff notarize or draft a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not write legal documents, and its own staff do not notarize what they record, since that would create a conflict of interest. The County Clerk's office next door has a notary available for a small fee.

faqs.q: What would a $100,000 sale owe in transfer tax?
faqs.a: $860 in total: $750 to the state and $110 to the county, according to the county's chart. A $200,000 sale would owe $1,720 at the same rates.
